title: Linearisation: The Tangent Plane Snaps On
topic: Linear approximation of a surface near a point. Around a point (a, b) the surface z = f(x, y) is well-approximated by the tangent plane L(x, y) = f(a, b) + f_x(a, b)(x - a) + f_y(a, b)(y - b). Up close the plane and the surface become indistinguishable — that's what differentiability means.

beats.narration: Up close, every smooth surface looks flat. Linearisation is the rule that turns that picture into a formula.

elements.content: Manimo bobs centre, caption 'Up close, flat.'

beats.narration: Take a single variable picture first. A curve, and a point on it. The tangent line at that point matches both the value and the slope of the curve.

elements.content: Smooth curve y = f(x), violet-400, drawn on chalk-300 axes
Marked point P = (a, f(a)) on the curve, chalk-100 dot
Tangent line at P, amber-400, drawn through the marked point
Right panel: 'one-variable case' eyebrow + L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a) + caption 'value and slope match at P'

beats.narration: Zoom in on the point. The curve and the tangent line drift apart only at second order, so for any small step they trace nearly the same height.

elements.content: Same curve and tangent — now drawn on a zoomed window around P, gap between them shrinks to nothing
A faint rose-400 bracket marks the local window
Right panel: 'zoom in' eyebrow + 'they share value, slope — they disagree only at the second order' caption

beats.narration: The two variable version reads the same. Match the value, match the x slope, match the y slope. That's the equation of the tangent plane.

elements.content: 'two variables — same idea' mono eyebrow centred top
Big serif formula: L(x, y) = f(a, b) + f_x(a, b)(x - a) + f_y(a, b)(y - b) with f_x in violet, f_y in teal, f(a,b) in chalk-100
Footnote 'value, x-slope, y-slope — all three locked in.'

beats.narration: Differentiability, in one sentence: the surface is well approximated by a plane.

elements.content: 'Smooth means flat at the point.' — serif italic 54px, 'flat' in amber-300
'The tangent plane is the surface's best linear copy.' — serif italic 26px
